chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not sever the throat of the sacrificial animal until it dies; when it has died, then sever its throat.' If his hand hastened and he severed it [before death], there is no objection to that, but that ruling is only for when it is done unintentionally; [if done intentionally], it is not permissible.

key_terms.نَخَعَ: To sever or cut (specifically the throat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on severing the animal's throat before it fully dies during slaughter?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the animal must be fully dead before the throat is severed for the slaughter to be valid, emphasizing the distinction between intentional and unintentional errors. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that validity is preserved in cases of inadvertence (khata'), whereas intentional deviation renders the meat impermissible, reflecting a nuanced approach to ritual purity and animal welfare.
